newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Everbright-IHD places shares.
newsitem.headline: China Everbright-IHD places shares.

text.p: China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd said its parent company had placed out existing shares, then subscribed for twice the number of new shares, providing funds for a stake in Theme International and other assets.

The company was currently in negotiations with Hong Kong-based retailer Theme to take a 20 percent stake in the company, but no agreement had been signed as yet, the company said in a statement published on Thursday.
Everbright-IHD also said in the statement it would like to acquire a 20 percent stake in Everbright Bank of China, which is 51 percent owned by ultimate parent China Everbright Group Ltd.
The required approvals allowing it to take a minority stake had been applied for but not yet received.
The company said controlling shareholder China Everbright Holding Co Ltd had placed out 87.7 million old shares at a price of HK$10.75 per placing share, the statement said.
The placing shares represent about 10 percent of the existing share capital of the company, the statement said.

The price is a 9.7 percent discount to the shares' closing price of HK$11.90 on Friday, May 23, and a premium of about 5.9 percent to the average closing price of the shares on the previous five trading days ending May 23, it said.
China Everbright Holdings also subscribed for a total of 175.55 million new shares in Everbright-IHD, it said.
These shares, issued at the price of HK$10.75, represented about 20 percent of the company's existing capital and 17 percent of the enlarged issued capital.
After the placement and issue of new shares, the parent company's stake in Everbright-IHD would be unchanged at 50.02 percent of the enlarged issued capital of the company.
At the placing price, the company's shares are valued at about 244 times the company's unaudited net profit of HK$38.7 million for the 12 months ended September 1996.

But they are valued at 69 times its pro forma earnings of HK$136.71 million, shown in accounts prepared at the time of the company's acquisition of a 20 percent stake in International Bank of Asia Ltd (IBA) and a five percent stake in National Mutual Asia Ltd in February.
